articleTitle: Investigation of Design Performance in Outer Rotor BLDC Motor for Taguchi Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper optimized the performance of an actual brushless DC electric fan motor with a rated power of 26 Watts by analyzing the simulation of this reference model. Optimization is made based on the Taguchi Method. This study primarily investigates an outer rotor BLDC motor design, and the parameters of interest include torque, output power, and efficiency. The characteristics of the physical brushless BLDC configurations are compared with the proposed design to evaluate the performance of the proposed model. Optimization results using the Taguchi Methods show that the proposed model outperforms the reference design regarding the specified parameters. The ability of the proposed motor simulation result can further be analyzed from its magnetics flux distribution and Finite Element Method (FEM). The paper also compares the characteristics of physical BLDC configurations with the proposed design.

articleTitle: Low-speed Sensorless Control of SPMSM based on Pulsated High Frequency Current Signal Injection and Detection Coils
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Sensorless control of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) is important for its system integration and cost reduction, for which the high frequency (HF) voltage injection method is generally utilized for its low speed performance. However, the bandwidth limitation and estimation error respectively due to additional filters and HF impedance variation still need improvement for the voltage injection method. In this paper, a novel HF current injection method is proposed to cope with the problems mentioned above for the surface permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM). The reduction of filter requirement and enhanced impedance robustness are analyzed theoretically, contributing to improved dynamic performance and estimation accuracy. which are also validated through simulations.

articleTitle: Design of Cooling System for High Torque Density Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Heat Pipe
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: To address the issue of excessive temperature rise in high-torque-density permanent magnet synchronous motors, a heat pipe cooling system is proposed. This system involves embedding heat pipes with high thermal conductivity into the motor’s end section. Finite element simulations were conducted on a 4-pole, 24-slot, surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor with a high torque density of 7.68 Nm/kg. An analysis was performed to compare the cooling capabilities of a traditional water cooling system and the heat pipe cooling system. The results demonstrate that the heat pipe efficiently dissipates the accumulated heat in the motor windings, reducing the temperature rise by 6.98°C compared to the traditional water cooling system. Furthermore, an optimization of the heat pipe’s geometric shape concludes that a bending angle of 30° for the heat pipe performs most reasonably, laying a foundation for the application of heat pipes in motor cooling systems.

articleTitle: The Relationship Between Pole Width and Load Capacity in Radial Magnetic Bearings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In the design process of radial magnetic bearings (RMBs), the maximum load capacity is a critical parameter. Under the condition of fixed stator inner and outer diameters, the maximum load capacity is closely related to the pole width. This article first derives the relationship between the two based on the ideal model. Furthermore, the saturation model is introduced to characterize the saturation of the iron core in practical cases, and a method is provided to determine the optimal pole width under different saturation magnetic flux density conditions. Based on the above analysis, finite element analysis (FEA) was employed for simulation, and the simulation results showed good agreement with the theoretical analysis results.

articleTitle: Design optimization of Outer-Rotor Surface-Mounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines Using Trapezoid Permanent Magnet Shape
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of an outer-rotor surface-mounted permanent magnet (OR-SPM) synchronous machine designed for integrated starter-generator (ISG) systems. The electromagnetic characteristics of OR-SPM machines using different PM shapes are analyzed and compared, including no-load behaviors, output torque, and torque ripple. This paper introduces a novel trapezoid-shaped PM for OR-SPM, distinct from the conventional ring-shaped PM. The optimization process employs a multi-objective genetic algorithm (MOGA) to optimize the geometrical parameters of the trapezoidal-shaped PM. The goal is to maximize the output torque while simultaneously minimizing the volume of PM, thereby enhancing the overall utilization of PM. Finite element analysis (FEA) is conducted on the two machines with the same rotor size and stator operating at the same rated current to validate the feasibility of the trapezoidal PM machine. The results demonstrate that the trapezoidal shape design effectively increases the output torque compared to the ring-shaped PM machine.

articleTitle: EMI Issues and Reduction in 800 V Electrical Vehicle Systems by Incorporating Cable Effects
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: As electric vehicles (EVs) evolve, there is a notable shift in battery voltage levels from the conventional 400V to an elevated 800V. This transition offers advantages such as faster charging times, reduced energy losses, and the potential for more compact motor designs. However, this comes with a trade-off: an increased rate of voltage change (dv/dt), which can exacerbate Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) issues. The presence of cables connecting the motor to the motor drive and battery packs can further amplify these EMI challenges. Therefore, this paper initially conducts a comparative analysis of EMI performance between 400 V and 800 V EV systems. Subsequently, we introduce a filter design methodology specifically tailored to mitigate EMI in 800V bus systems. The efficacy of the proposed filter design is substantiated through both simulations and experimental results, confirming its role in effective EMI reduction with 20 dB reduction.

articleTitle: Optimization of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor for Industrial Ceiling Fans Based on Differential Evolutionary Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this paper a 72-slot, 60-pole, high-torque, low-speed external rotor permanent magnet synchronous motor, which is aiming to fulfill the industrial large-scale ceiling fans’ demands for high torque density and minimal torque pulsation, is designed. A targeted optimization is also conducted on the motor. Given the structural properties of the permanent magnet synchronous motor, it naturally produces cogging torque. This can result in the motor’s torque ripple, vibration, and noise, particularly noticeable at low speeds. Consequently, implementing methods to reduce this cogging torque is highly significant. The paper employs a differential evolutionary algorithm to enhance a multi-objective motor design scheme and the corresponding optimization scheme is proposed. It involves tuning pole-slot coordination and adjusting motor parameters, all while reducing the cogging torque and maintaining output torque under load condition. The effectiveness of the motor design is ultimately confirmed through finite element simulation under various working conditions.

Author Keywords: External rotor permanent magnet synchronous motor

articleTitle: Predictive Control of Five-leg Inverter Driving Dual PMSMs for Overcurrent Suppression
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The five-leg inverter has been investigated widely as a low-cost solution for dual permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) drives. For this topology, the overcurrent issue of the shared leg should be carefully considered. In the paper, a novel model predictive control (MPC) scheme is presented to realize independent dual-PMSMs control, effective overcurrent elimination, and fast transient response simultaneously. A classical duty cycle partitioning scheme is adopted to decouple the association of each motor drive. The overcurrent component is contained in the cost function design directly. Moreover, a master-slave structure is utilized to coordinate the current phase angle relationship and keep dual PMSMs running synchronously. Finally, a simulation of three-PMSMs system is executed, and the obtained results substantiate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Multi-Physics Coupled Analysis and Global Optimization of High Power Density Permanent Magnet Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: High power density machines have attracted increasing attention, but they are reaching the thermal and mechanical limits of the materials, bringing challenges to the machine designs. In this paper, a reliable and effective multi-physics coupling analysis is integrated to the global optimization based on genetic algorithm, to improve the optimization efficiency. The basic modeling on fluid, temperature, electromagnetic, and mechanical fields are introduced, and their couplings as well as the general optimization process are highlighted. Afterwards, a cased study based on the surface-mounted permanent magnet (SPM) machine with the rated power of 15 kW at the speed of 20000 r/min is detailed to describe the optimization process.

articleTitle: Quantitative Evaluation Method of Moisture of Oil-paper Insulation Based on Frequency-dependent Characteristic of The Dielectric Response Current
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In order to ensure the safe and reliable operation of high voltage power equipment, it is important to evaluate the moisture content of oil paper insulation accurately. At present, the evaluation of insulation properties of oil-paper is mostly based on frequency domain spectroscopy (FDS) to achieve the estimation of moisture content, while ignoring the information carried by the response current itself in the test process. Given this issue, the f-I<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> curve is proposed to characterize the moisture state of oil-paper insulation, and the characteristic parameter in the curve can be used to evaluate the moisture of oil paper insulation. The results show that the f-I<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> curve presents a straight line under dry condition, and gradually becomes a concave with the increase of moisture state degree. And use the f-I<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> curve to assess that the moisture content of the oil-paper insulation will not be affected by the excitation voltage and the degree of polymerization of insulating paper. And by using the I<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> value at 50 Hz of f-I<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> curve, the moisture degree of oil-paper insulation can be quantitatively evaluated, and the moisture of the actual oil-immersed equipment is evaluated. The results are consistent with the overall rule obtained by IDAX-300 test, which verifies the feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: Power Decoupling Micro-inverse Control for Singlephase PV Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Addressing the critical issue of frequency doubling on the DC link in single-phase grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) systems, this paper introduces a power decoupling technique. The proposed method, integrating an additional phase leg, effectively neutralizes the detrimental impacts of frequency doubling on system efficiency and reliability. This technique can also realize multiplexing, simplifying the circuitry. The effectiveness of this method can be evaluated by using MATLAB/Simulink model for simulation, obtaining simulation results and carrying out corresponding analysis and processing. Results indicate a pronounced decrease in DC link ripple energy and the potential for reducing energy storage dimensions.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Model of Hysteresis Motor Considering Magnetic Field Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Hysteresis motor has received extensive attention recently because of its excellent characteristics in some aspects. However, the nonlinear and multi-valued properties of hysteresis materials make the performance evaluation of hysteresis motors more complicated, and the previous calculation model based on elliptic approximation of hysteresis loops does not take into account the influence of harmonics and is not accurate enough. Based on the equivalent circuit model, this paper introduces the consideration of magnetic field harmonics, so as to improve the calculation accuracy of magnetic field distribution and steady-state torque. On this basis, the factors affecting the performance of hysteresis motor can be analyzed.

articleTitle: Analytical Calculation of Loaded Torque for SPM Machines Based on an Improved Equivalent Surface Current Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In order to calculate the torque of the parallel magnetized eccentric pole shaping surface-mounted permanent magnet (SPM) machines under different load conditions accurately and quickly, an improved equivalent surface current method is used to treat the PM, and the loaded air-gap magnetic field of the SPM machines is calculated by combining the subdomain method and superposition principle. The surface of PMs is divided into several infinitesimals by the improved equivalent surface current method, each representing a currentcarrying conductor. The current value and position of each current-carrying conductor can be easily solved by transforming the local coordinate system into the global coordinate system. Therefore, the improved equivalent surface current method has the advantages of simple calculation and fast computation speed. The analytical method is used to calculate the torque under different loaded conditions, and the correctness of the analytical calculation is verified by comparing it with the finite-element analysis and the experimental method.

articleTitle: A Novel Magnetization State Manipulation Strategy for Isolated Dual Three-Phase Variable Flux Memory Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The variable flux memory (VFM) motor can realize the online re-magnetization and demagnetization via d-axis armature current pulses. However, the corresponding pulse currents during magnetization state (MS) regulation lead to significant pulsating torque and speed fluctuations. In this paper, based on the segregated dual three-phase (DTP) VFM (DTP-VFM) motor, a new PM MS manipulation method based on step-by-step dual d-axis current pulses in single winding set, is proposed. The new method is compared with the traditional method based on dual-winding sets. The results reveal that the new step-by-step MS manipulation strategy is not only effective, but also exhibits enhanced pulsating torque and speed fluctuation suppression effect.

articleTitle: A Fault-Tolerant Control Strategy for Open-Circuit Faults in the Active Rectifier of the Doubly Salient Electromagnetic Generation System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In the conventional doubly salient electromagnetic generation (DSEG) system, the output is rectified by a diode rectifier. Active rectifiers with angular position control (APC) can significantly improve the output capacity and efficiency of the DSEG system. Although the possibility of fault is higher, active rectifiers extend the scope of fault-tolerant control. Active rectifier faults can lead to the reduction in the output capacity and efficiency. The characteristics of the DSEG system are analyzed during normal operation and after the occurrence of three types of open-circuit faults in the single-phase lower bridge arm of the active rectifier. A fault-tolerant control strategy is proposed for open-circuit faults. The results show that the fault-tolerant control strategy can restore the output capacity and efficiency of the DSEG system to some extent.

articleTitle: Ripple Reduction of Electromagnetic Supporting Force in Aerodynamic Bearing-Equipped SPMSM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: A high-speed surface mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM) equipped with aerodynamic bearings is studied in this paper. Controllable electromagnetic supporting force (EMSF) is produced by the motor armature windings, while electromagnetic torque being simultaneously generated, in order to mitigate dry friction in the air bearings before reaching the lift-off speed of the bearings. During this process, smooth output of the EMSF directly impacts the dry friction reduction. However, the EMSF also does exhibit ripples. Hence, in this paper a new method is proposed to reduce the ripple from the perspective of machine electromagnetic design. Firstly, the principle of generating the constant EMSF is deduced and the EMSF ripple is investigated. Taking a four-pole machine as an illustrative example, the spatial harmonics of the air gap magnetic field, which increases the EMSF ripple, are analyzed. Then, to suppress the harmonic components contributing dominantly to the EMSF ripple, a permanent magnet (PM) pole shaping method is proposed, by which the dominant harmonics are reduced. Conversely, harmonic components which have a relatively minor effect on the EMSF ripple are injected into the PM. The optimal composition of the harmonics is calculated to enhance the fundamental component content under the same magnetic thickness. Finally, the reduction effect of the EMSF ripple is validated with the finite element analysis results.

Author Keywords: Surface Mounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor

articleTitle: Characterization of a novel counter-rotating twin harmonic PM machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Most machine topologies have two-ports, with one set of electrical connections and one mechanical shaft. Three-port machines having two rotors and mechanical shafts are able to drive two mechanical loads using one stator winding, fed by one power converter. In addition, it is possible to get the mechanical shafts to counter-rotate, which is promising for applications such as marine propulsion and hydraulic pumps. In this paper, a three-port radial flux permanent magnet machine is presented. A 2kW technology demonstrator based on this design is built, and its characteristics are presented, including the back-emf voltage waveforms. The phase sequence of the back-emf of each rotor shows that counter-rotation is possible using one stator winding. Next to that, a no-load motor test confirmed that when feeding a sinusoidal voltage to one stator winding, it is possible to have two mechanically counter-rotating rotors.

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Transient Simulation of 500kV Unified Power Flow Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: As the most versatile flexible AC transmission system to date, the unified power flow controller(UPFC) not only controls the AC line power flow, but also provides reactive power compensation to the system. At present, UPFC has been developed to 500 kV voltage level, and the converters’ structure is modular multilevel converter(MMC). The special structure of UPFC’s series side transformer makes the control strategy and fault characteristics of UPFC different from the existing MMC-HVDC project, and electromagnetic transient simulation research is urgently needed. Based on the published data of 500 kV UPFC project in Suzhou Southern Power Grid, this paper conducts electromagnetic transient simulation research on 500 kV MMCUPFC in PSCAD, which can provide support for the control strategy, protection scheme and the overvoltage and insulation cooperation of UPFC.

articleTitle: Analysis of Torque Characteristics of Built-in Uneven Air Gap Permanent Magnet Synchronous Direct Drive Motor for Heavy Duty Locomotive
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In order to meet the demand of high torque density and stable operation of permanent magnet synchronous direct drive motor (PMSDDM) for heavy load locomotive, the rotor structure with uneven air gap was used to improve the amplitude of air gap magnetic field fundamental wave, so as to improve the electromagnetic torque and reduce the cogging torque of PMSDDM. The uneven air gap ratio k, the ratio of maximum air gap to minimum air gap, was scanned by finite element simulation software. By comparing the fundamental wave amplitude of air gap magnetic field, cogging torque and electromagnetic torque under different values of k, the trend of their changing with k were obtained, so the optimal value of k was determined. The simulation results showed that the reasonable uneven air gap can improve the electromagnetic torque of PMSDDM, at the same time reduce the amplitude of the cogging torque. The performance of PMSDDM was improved.

articleTitle: Study on Estimation Method of Stray Inductance and Its Influence on Switching Loss for SiC MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs offer notable benefits such as fast switching time and low switching losses. However, the quick switching characteristics of SiC MOSFETs can generate high rates of dv/dt and di/dt, with the presence of stray inductance, giving rise to voltage and current oscillations. To address this issue, a novel method has been proposed to accurately estimate the stray inductance originating from wires or component leads. This method enables the determination of the ratio of each stray inductance to the loop inductance. Consequently, the switching characteristics are analyzed under different stray inductance from different lead lengths. The validity of these findings has been confirmed by experimental results.

articleTitle: A Smooth and Fast I/f Control Method for PMSM Startup by Current Compensation Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Sensorless control of permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM) has been well applied in many industrial applications due to its cost reduction and mechanical simplicity. The back-EMF based sensorless control has poor performance in low-speed range. Therefore in some applications where low-speed accurate control is not required, I/f control method is used for startup and switching to back-EMF-based sensorless control. During the startup, a large load torque disturbance causes large speed fluctuation and lead to oscillation even out of synchronism. This paper analyzes the causes and influencing factors of speed fluctuation, and based on that a control method by current compensation during startup is proposed The proposed method can be effectively applied to reduce the speed ripples without extending the startup time.

articleTitle: A Novel Deadtime Compensation Strategy Based on Current Ripple Estimation Combined with Drive Pulse Width
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In voltage-source inverters (VSIs), deadtime is used to prevent going straight through over switching devices. However, the existence of the deadtime will distort the output phase current, which degrades the performance of VSIs. The traditional drive pulse width correction is developed by analyzing the effects of deadtime on a pulse by pulse basis and correcting each pulse according to the polarity of phase current. Given that common sampling-based deadtime compensation (DTC) methods are often affected by current ripple. In this paper, we introduce a novel DTC method for VSIs that eliminates the effect of current ripple and improves the accuracy of DTC.The proposed strategy reconstructs the current values at the turn-on and turn-off moments of the drive signals for each phase in real-time by calculating the current ripple trajectory. Simulations and experiments are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Torque Ripple Suppression Of Permanent Magnet Brushless DC Frameless Torque Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper analyzes the effects of different slot-pole combinations, unequal-magnet height poles, motor structural parameters, and permanent magnet parameters on torque ripple by finite element simulation. In order to cope with the working condition of a permanent magnet brushless DC frameless torque motor (PMFTM) sensitive to speed fluctuations in a robot drive system, the 39-slot/12-pole frameless motor is taken as an example. Two eccentric pole structures were selected for the analysis of air gap magnetism and radial electromagnetism, as well as their impact on vibration noise. Furthermore, a multi-objective genetic algorithm based on sensitivity analysis method is introduced to obtain the optimal torque and torque ripple. The simulation results demonstrate that the designed motor exhibits excellent performance in terms of cogging torque and suppression of ripple torque.

articleTitle: Motor Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on Fourier-based Synchrosqueezing Transform and Hilbert Envelope Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Motor’s current signal contains information about its operation status and thus can be used to diagnose motor bearing faults. To solve the problem that the stator current changes are generally subtle and the traditional signal processing methods cannot accurately extract the signal fault characteristic frequency, this paper proposes a stator-current-based motor bearing fault diagnosis method based on Fourier-based Synchrosqueezing Transform (FSST) and Hilbert envelope spectrum. The method uses FSST to decompose the signal into a set of Intrinsic Mode Function (IMF) components containing bearing fault characteristic information, selects the appropriate IMF components for current signal reconstruction, and then combines the Hilbert envelope spectrum with the spectrum analysis of the reconstructed signals to obtain a clear fault characteristic frequency. Compared with the traditional method, the proposed method effectively suppresses modal mixing and noise interference, improving the effectiveness and accuracy of fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Improved Estimation of Non-Sinusoidal Back-EMF with Kalman Filter Applied to Surface-Mounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)

authors.preferredName: Stefan Thiago C. A. Dos Santos
José Roberto B. De A. Monteiro

abstract: The back-electromotive force (back-EMF) estimation with the Kalman filter can be applied to the sensorless control of surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous machines. The adoption of different back-EMF waveform dynamics modeling in the system model affects the estimation performance. This work proposes an improved estimation of non-sinusoidal back-EMF using the Kalman filter algorithm, which considers the actual back-EMF dynamics on the system model; hence, this choice relies on the previous knowledge of the back-EMF waveform. The proposed approach is compared to two other methods present in the literature. Simulation results show a more than 90% reduction in the estimation integral absolute error (IAE) compared to the case when the back-EMF dynamics are neglected and up to 80% when the back-EMF is considered sinusoidal. Accordingly, an improvement in the orientation angle estimation is also noticeable, especially for the lower evaluated speed operating point whose IAE reduction was higher than 60%.

articleTitle: Investigation of Vernier Machine Design with Hybrid Excitations and Ferrite Magnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Recently, the fluctuating costs of rare earth materials have led to an increased interest in exploring alternative non-rare earth materials. The goal is to reduce costs in various applications. Among these applications, direct drive motors have received significant attention for their enhanced performance, and the vernier motor has emerged as a promising candidate due to its flux-modulation working principle. Nonetheless, the vernier motor’s drawback of a low power factor has been the subject of research investigation. Additionally, the utilization of rare-earth magnets unavoidably leads to increased costs. The utilization of a hybrid-excited winding in this study demonstrates its potential to enhance the power factor of the vernier motors. Additionally, this innovative approach offers another noteworthy advantage: an improved field weakening capability. These findings highlight the promising prospects of employing the hybrid-excited winding as an effective solution to optimize motor performance and achieve better energy efficiency in various applications.

articleTitle: Novel Design Method of Flux-Barrier End Shape of Synchronous Reluctance Motor Based on B-spline Curves
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: By introducing the widely used B-spline curves, commonly employed in computer graphics, to the rotor topology optimization, this paper presents a novel design method for the flux-barrier end of the synchronous reluctance (SynRel) motor. This novel approach offers enhanced flexibility in shape design along with powerful parametric expression. The flux-barrier end significantly impacts the electromagnetic and stress performance of the rotor, thus playing an important role in the designs for achieving smoother operation, higher efficiency and a more robust structure. Several papers have already proposed some simple but reasonable methods for better flux-barrier shape. This paper illustrates details and performance comparisons between traditional and new designs. Then a SynRel motor with B-spline Curve flux-barrier end is provided with comprehensive improvement in torque, torque ripple, efficiency and stress distribution. Sensitivity analysis is conducted for guidelines of design. Electro-mechanical co-optimization is performed using finite element analysis (FEA), surrogate models, nature-inspired algorithms and multi-level optimization. Additionally, several motors with enhanced performance are presented in the end. In conclusion, the utilization of B-spline curves in the design of flux-barrier ends contribute to achieve greater efficiency in design and performance improvements in terms of torque ripple and stress distribution.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Wide Speed-Regulated Reverse Salient-Pole Variable Leakage Flux Interior Permanent Magnet Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: A novel wide speed-regulated reverse salient-pole variable leakage flux interior permanent magnet (RSP-VLF-IPM) machine is proposed, in this paper. The unique advantage of the proposed motor, in contrast to the conventional interior permanent magnet (IPM) motor with a constant permanent magnet field, is the ability to control the leakage flux by armature magnetomotive force. Additionally, the proposed motor can operate in the region where the magnetic field is enhanced due to its reverse salient-pole characteristic. To elaborate on the working principle of the RSP-VLF-IPM machine, a magnetic circuit analysis is conducted. Furthermore, the performance of the two motors is reasonably analysis using 2D finite element analysis. The simulation results show that the proposed motor offers a wider speed range and higher efficiency.

articleTitle: Vibration Suppression for PMSM Flexible Servo Systems Using Enhanced Two-Mode Shapers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Due to the flexibility of loads, multi-mode vibration is excited by rapid motion during servo positioning, which poses significant hazards to industrial production. This article provides a clear explanation of the mechanism behind vibration generation when driving flexible loads with permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs). A novel vibration suppression method based on enhanced two-mode shapers is proposed. The proposed method effectively suppresses the first two vibration modes that have the most significant impact on servo control. This method is designed for flexible servo systems with a large mode ratio where conventional input shapers are not suitable. The effectiveness of the proposed method was verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Design of High Torque Density Magnetic Gear Composite Motor for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Electric vehicles are the focus of the country to solve the energy crisis and environmental pollution problems. At present, electric vehicles often use the combination of motor and gear transmission system, there are problems such as low system efficiency and poor reliability, which limits the further development of electric vehicles. To solve this problem, a kind of magnetic gear composite motor with high torque density is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the structural characteristics of the motor are described and its main parameters are designed. Then the operating mechanism of the motor is derived based on the magnetic field modulation theory. Finally, the effects of different magnetization methods on motor performance are compared and analyzed. The results show that the designed high torque density magnetic gear composite motor has good operation performance, which can provide a new idea for the design of drive motor for electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Topology Construction Method of Hybrid PMs Variable Flux Memory Machine Based on Magnetic Circuit Structure Evolution
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this article, the rules and internal structural relationship of mutual evolution among different magnetic circuit (MC) structures of hybrid PMs variable flux memory machines (VFMMs) are studied, and a topology construction method based on MC structure evolution is proposed. This method can rapidly expand the topological database in the form of multiples, which provides a sufficient population for seeking the topology that can achieve the optimal balance among the various electromagnetic characteristics of VFMM. The MC structures that can form a symmetrical magnetic electromotive force distribution under different PMs numbers are explored, and the mutual evolution rules of different MC structures are further revealed. On this basis, the proposed topology construction method is introduced. Using this method, a series MC VFMM is evolved into two topological structures with different MC forms. Subsequently, to determine the topology structures with the best performance balance, their key electromagnetic characteristics are analyzed and compared respectively. Finally, the experiment of an evolved hybrid MC VFMM prototype verifies the feasibility and effectiveness of constructing more VFMM with novel topology and superior electromagnetic performance through MC structure evolution.

articleTitle: Comparison of Two Auxiliary Suspension Winding Configurations for High-Speed SPMSM with Aerodynamic Bearings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Aerodynamic bearings are one type of non-contact bearings without air supply. However, the dry friction and the instability problem of the bearings put forward the need for external intervention. To provide the aerodynamic bearing with an external electromagnetic force, an auxiliary suspension winding is additionally inserted in the stator core slots of a surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM), which works like that of the bearingless motor. To generate a controllable radial force, there are two topologies for the inserted auxiliary suspension winding. For a 4-armature-pole motor, the auxiliary suspension winding can be of either 2-pole or 6-pole. In this paper, auxiliary suspension winding structure and radial force generation principle in the 4-pole SPMSM are detailed, and comparison in several aspects between two different auxiliary suspension winding topologies for the same 4-pole SPMSM will be discussed. Moreover, analytical derivation and finite element method (FEM) verification are elaborated.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Design and Optimization of High-Speed Solid-Rotor Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: High-speed solid-rotor induction motors (HSSRIM) are widely used in industrial applications due to their simple structure and high rotor strength. This paper discusses the electromagnetic design and optimization process of a 15kW-120,000rpm HSSRIM. The finite element method (FEM) is used to validate and preliminarily optimize the electromagnetic design. By analyzing the influencing factors of the selected target, the motor parameters (stator outer diameter, axial length, stator groove depth, stator groove width) which have great influence on the target are determined as the optimization variables. Then the response surface model of type Kriging and multi-objective genetic (MOGA) algorithm are used for optimization. The output power and the ratio of starting torque to rated torque are constrained to ensure that the results meet the basic performance requirements. Then the motor structure is optimized to maximize the steady-state efficiency. Finally, the stator core loss is reduced, and the power factor, efficiency and starting performance of the motor are improved.

articleTitle: Optimal Frequency Design Method of IPT System Based on Power Loss Model for Rail Transit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Recently, inductive power transfer (IPT) system has developed rapidly. However, there is currently no optimal frequency design method for IPT system applied in rail transit, lacking theoretical and practical support based on systematic in-depth research. Therefore, this paper proposes an optimal frequency design method for IPT system applied in rail transit. The optimal frequency is determined by establishing the power loss model of the IPT system. Based on theoretical analysis, this paper offers guidelines in selecting the optimum frequency. A 30 kW IPT system prototype for maglev train is built to confirm the theoretical results. It is concluded that when the length of the transmitting coil is 5 m, the efficiency of the IPT system is the highest for the operating frequency of 29.1 kHz.

articleTitle: Sensorless Vector Control for Induction Motor Startup Using Multilevel Converters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Multilevel converters are increasingly viewed as the next generation of motor drives, offering advantages such as reduced harmonics, enhanced electromagnetic interference (EMI) performance, and greater flexibility and scalability in voltage and current levels. Despite these benefits, a significant challenge arises during the startup of induction motors driven by multilevel converters, primarily due to AC voltage fluctuations in the DC capacitors of each submodule. Additionally, the use of voltage sensors, while commonly, introduces potential points of failure and increases overall system costs. To address these issues, this paper presents a novel sensorless vector control strategy based on speed and phase angle estimation. The proposed method has been empirically verified to achieve successful startup with accurate speed estimation and minimal AC voltage fluctuation.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of a High-Speed Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor with Stator Auxiliary Slots Based on Multi-Physics Field Coupling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: High-speed permanent magnet synchronous motors (HSPMSM) have excellent dynamic performance. But the harmonics in its high-frequency alternating magnetic field also cause additional losses, making its losses much higher than those of a normal-speed motor. Adding auxiliary slots can attenuate the harmonics, but how to optimize the auxiliary slots according to their size and shape has not been studied. To better explore the influence of the auxiliary slot and improve the efficiency of optimizing the HSPMSM, this paper optimizes the topology of a 15 kW, 120,000 rpm HSPMSM. The optimized HSPMSM is calibrated based on multi-physics field simulation, and the results show that the optimized scheme can significantly suppress harmonics and effectively reduce the loss density of the HSPMSM without affecting the output performance of the HSPMSM.

articleTitle: LUT-based Modelling of PMSMs Considering Spatial Harmonics, Interturn Short-Circuit Faults, and Zero-Sequence Components
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper presents a general model for permanent-magnet synchronous machines (surface-mounted or interior permanent-magnet) considering both space harmonics, interturn short-circuit faults and zero-sequence components. First, the healthy machine model is obtained. Magnetic saturation is disregarded such that the machine inductances depend only on the rotor position, allowing for a relatively straightforward derivation of the relations between flux-linkages, torque, currents, and rotor position. Secondly, the faulty machine model is derived assuming that the effect of the precise position of the interturn short-circuit inside the slot is negligible. Thirdly, the latter model is upgraded with an artificial neural network to account for the relative position of the interturn short-circuit. Finally, all the presented models are validated based on a finite-element analysis.

articleTitle: Control Strategy for Fault Tolerance in Semi-Active Multi-Module Range-Extended Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Range-extended electric vehicles (REEVs), combining attributes of hybrid and pure electric models, present a promising solution to address challenges associated with the widespread adoption of pure electric vehicles. These challenges include high costs, limited energy density, long charging times, and range anxiety. REEVs hold significant potential for diverse applications. However, current research on REEVs predominantly focuses on parameter optimization and energy management strategies, overlooking the critical aspect of the vehicle's fault tolerance and resilience in applications such as long-distance cargo transportation, military operations, and medical emergency services. This paper introduces a modular-based design for a multi-module range-extended electric vehicle and its faulttolerant operational control strategy, ensuring seamless vehicle operation and mission completion in demanding scenarios.

articleTitle: Identification of VSI Nonlinearity of Variable Flux Memory Machine Based on PM Flux Linkage Disturbance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The nonlinearity inherent in the voltage source inverter (VSI) causes a deviation between the desired reference voltage and the actual output voltage of the VSI, which is particularly evident during the low-speed operation stage of the motor. In this paper, a novel approach is presented for online estimation of VSI nonlinearity by manipulating the permanent magnet (PM) flux linkage of the variable flux memory machine (VFMM). First, a voltage estimation model based on PM flux linkage disturbance considering VSI nonlinearity is developed. Second, based on this, in order to mitigate the impact caused by the error in rotor position, this method employs the dc components of q-axis equation and the observed PM flux linkage of VFMM to estimate the value of VSI-distorted voltage. The estimated distortion voltage is then fed back to the reference voltage to compensate for the nonlinearity of the VSI, thereby improving the dynamic performance of the system. The simulation results validate the effectiveness and viability of the proposed novel estimation approach.

articleTitle: Finding Grounding Points in Substation DC System by DC Current Injection Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The operation environment of the secondary circuit of the substation is poor, which is easy to cause grounding failure. Once the two-point grounding, there is a risk of automatic device rejection or misoperation, which needs to be eliminated as soon as possible when the single point grounding. However, the efficiency of the early search method is low, which is easy to cause the wrong action of the relay protection equipment. The AC injection method commonly used at present will cause disturbance to the secondary circuit, which is easy to be interfered by distributed capacitance. DC leakage current monitoring method has a large input and can not locate the fault point. The DC current injection method is proposed in this paper, which can overcome the influence of the charge and discharge transient of distributed capacitors. The DC constant current is used to charge distributed capacitors for a short time, and stable and continuous current is formed in the circuit where the grounding fault is located after the steady state is reached. The DC clamp ammeter is used to efficiently determine the faulty branch and quickly locate the specific grounding fault point on the branch. High security and reliability. At the same time, the method adopts constant current DC source, which can overcome the ground fault resistance fluctuation and has strong anti-interference ability.

articleTitle: A Method to Suppress Noise in Position Sensorless Control of PMSM Based on High-Frequency Signal Injection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this paper, an improved sensorless control method based on high-frequency square-wave signal injection of PMSM is proposed. The frequency spectrum of high-frequency current is expanded by injecting random-frequency and high-frequency square-wave voltage into the d-axis, thereby reducing audible noise. The optimal amplitude of the injected voltage is investigated. This paper designs and verifies the optimization program by calculating the root-mean-square error of the selected estimates. The performance of the proposed method is verified through MATLAB/Simulink simulation.

articleTitle: An Active Damping Method for IPMSM Drive with Small Film DC-Link Capacitor Based on Rectifier Side Current Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The LC resonance generated by the grid side inductor and the dc-link capacitor is a significant concern for the interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) drives with small film capacitor, which degrades the grid side power quality such as grid side current harmonics and input power factor. In this paper, an active damping method based on the rectifier side current is proposed to deal with the concern. The circuit model of the drive has been established to investigate the LC resonance and the instability issue. Different feedback variables are analyzed in detail and the rectifier side current is chosen, which is consistent with the LC resonance component in the grid side current. Meanwhile, a rectifier side current reconstruction method is proposed without adding extra sensors or sampling circuit hardware. The grid current harmonics can be suppressed and the input power factor is further improved. Experiments on an IPMSM drive have been carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A New Rotor Slotting Method for Reducing the Vibration and Noise of IPMSMs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this paper, a new rotor slotting method is proposed to reduce the vibration and noise of interior permanent-magnet synchronous machines (IPMSMs). By using the proposed rotor slotting method, new harmonic components are introduced into the air-gap permeance, reducing the specific radial electromagnetic force density (REFD) and concentrated radial force (CRF), and finally the machine’s vibration is reduced. After applying the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II (NSGA-II), the optimal slot location, number and size to achieve the best vibration weakening results can be found. On this basis, the vibration performance of a 12-slot 10-pole IPMSM is investigated with the proposed rotor slotting method.

articleTitle: Optimised CEEMDAN based on sparrow search algorithm for Motor Bearing Fault Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: For fault diagnosis, it is very important to extract effective fault feature information.Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN) is widely used in fault diagnosis due to its advantages of fast decomposition speed, good completeness of results, and high adaptivity. However, when the added Gaussian white noise is not suitable, it will still be affected by problems such as modal aliasing and component signal distortion, which increase the difficulty of diagnosis. In this paper, the Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA) is used to find out the optimal Gaussian white noise amplitude and the number of additions required for different fault information, so as to optimise the processing capability of CEEMDAN and achieve more accurate fault diagnosis. The experimental results show that this method suppresses the interference of modal aliasing and spurious components to a certain extent, and enhances the effectiveness of bearing fault feature extraction.

Author Keywords: Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise

articleTitle: Fast Design Methodology for Synchronous Reluctance Machine Rotor with Circular Flux Barriers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Parametrization of rotor topology in synchronous reluctance machines (SynRM), particularly those with circular flux barriers, has been explored through two distinct approaches. The one with a classic model offers limited parameters, constraining design flexibility, while the other with a complete model of non-concentric barriers provides extensive design freedom at the cost of increased parameters to be optimized and potential superfluous geometries. It is essential to find a fast and effective way for rotor parametrization besides these two approaches. In this paper, a new rotor parametrization method is proposed, based on partly-concentric circular flux barriers and an equation revealed between key parameters. It exhibits a design freedom between the classic model with concentric flux barriers and the complete model with non-concentric ones. A simple but efficient equation is introduced to enlarge the parameter scan range while avoiding useless and unfeasible rotor geometries, making the method more time-efficient. The three methods are adopted to parameterize and optimize a same SynRM. Predesigned end angles of the flux barriers are introduced in the integer-slot machines to help reduce the number of parameters while maintaining a high optimization performance. At last, the performances of the optimized machines obtained from the three models are compared, validating the fastness and effectiveness of the proposed design methodology.

articleTitle: Package Design of Three-Level Power Modules Based on Highly Integrated RC-IGBTs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Three-level power module with higher power density is widely used in photovoltaic power generation, motor drive and other fields. In order to solve the problem that the three-level module requires many components and has a complex structure, A new power module combining 1200V/400A RC-IGBT (Reverse-conducting insulated gate bipolar transistor) chip and A-NPC (Active Neutral Point Clamped) three-level topology is designed. RC-IGBT can meet real-time current and temperature monitoring and feedback, with high functional integration. Q3D and ANSYS simulation platforms were used to verify the rationality of module chip layout, package heat dissipation performance and mechanical reliability.

articleTitle: A Staggered Design of E-Scooters for Autonomous Deployment and Collection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to enhance the automated collection and deployment of e-scooters. This is achieved through the introduction of a novel staggered configuration for paired e-scooters, the development of a new steering mechanism, and the creation of a differential driving scheme. The study starts by exploring three distinct paired e-scooter designs and subsequently identifies the staggered configuration as the most feasible choice. To further substantiate this discovery and establish a foundation for future autonomous driving algorithms, the paper introduces the Staggered Ackermann Steering Geometry along with the formulas for calculating precise steering angles for the left and right staggered front wheels. Additionally, a novel differential driving scheme for the two staggered rear wheels is developed to enhance overall functionality. The proposed steering and driving algorithms undergo validation through experimental tests utilizing a dedicated test cart. The results confirm the potential for more efficient and stable autonomous driving of e-scooter pairs, providing a promising solution for the future of urban mobility.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Design of High-Speed Interior Permanent Magnet Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this paper, the electromagnetic design of a high-speed interior permanent magnet (IPM) is proposed. During the design process, not only the electromagnetic and loss characteristics of the high-speed IPM motor, but also the maximum stress of the rotor should be considered. First, the influence of rotor design parameters, including magnetic bridge thickness, rib width and stiffener thickness, on no-load back-EMF and rotor stress is analyzed. Then, the influence of the thickness and width of the PM on the motor rated-load performance and the maximum rotor stress is analyzed, based on the rotor structure of the PM in three segments. Finally, the electromagnetic properties and rotor stresses of the motor are verified by the finite element model.

articleTitle: Weak magnetic control of PMSM servo system with high bandwidth current loop
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The current sampling and pulse width modulation (PWM) duty cycle update methods currently in use in permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) servo control systems introduce significant delays, thereby impacting the motor’s current loop bandwidth and dynamic characteristics to some extent. In addition, when the motor terminal voltage reaches the maximum output voltage of the driver, the motor operating speed cannot continue to increase. In response to these issues, a current loop bandwidth expansion method was proposed by improving the current sampling and PWM update time. This method reduces the delay between current sampling and the PWM duty cycle update by advancing the timing of the PWM duty cycle update, thereby expanding the closed-loop bandwidth of the current loop control system. Building upon a high-bandwidth current loop, a variable q-axis single current regulator weak field control method is employed to enhance the speed of the PMSM further, ensuring stable operation beyond the base speed. The simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the newly designed bandwidth expansion method exhibits a reduced internal delay in the current loop of the AC permanent magnet servo control system compared to the existing sampling methods. Additionally, it offers a broader bandwidth and faster dynamic response. Combined with the weak magnetic control method, the control system has good stability, accuracy, and speed when operating above the base speed.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a Permanent Magnet Brushless DC Machine With Auxiliary Stator Slots
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This article investigates the impact of stator auxiliary slots on the performance and loss distributions of a permanent magnet brushless DC (PMBLDC) machine. Multiple designs of the machine prototype with stator auxiliary slots placed at different positions are investigated in-depth. Firstly, the influence of stator auxiliary slots on the PMBLDC machine air gap magnetic flux density is investigated by considering different machine design cases. Next, the output torque, cogging torque, back-EMF, and torque ripple response are analyzed and compared for the different machine design cases. The loss distributions for the machine design with auxiliary slots are also extensively researched. Lastly, an optimization analysis is conducted by investigating the impact of stator auxiliary slot dimensions, numbers, and position on the machine performance to obtain an optimized design solution for the PMBLDC machine.

articleTitle: Maximum Torque Per Ampere Control of IPMSM Based on Online Parameter Identification Considering Cross-coupling and Saturation effects
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In order to realize high-precision torque output and high-efficiency operation in new energy vehicle applications, maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) control is adopted below the base speed. However, due to the cross-coupling and saturation effects, the parameters of interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) change nonlinearly at different current operating points. The traditional MTPA control method has the calculation error of the target torque to current vector due to the uncertainty of motor parameters. To deal with the drawback of the traditional MTPA control, this paper proposed an MTPA control method based on online parameter identification. Based on dual frequency current signal injection, the dynamic inductance and flux linkage parameters are simply and effectively identified. And through the Newton’s method, the calculation of the current vector under the MTPA control considering the parameter change is realized. Simulation verifies the superiority of the proposed MTPA control method over the traditional method.

articleTitle: MTPA Control for Scalar Controlled Synchronous Reluctance Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Scalar control of synchronous reluctance motors (SynRMs) does not require precise position information and is less affected by magnetic circuit saturation. But the scalar control is easy to out of step and has low efficiency. To solve the problems above, this paper presents an efficient SynRM I/F control method. The speed of current vector is adjusted by the active power, and the amplitude of current vector is adjusted by the approximate position observation. The simulation results prove that compared with ordinary I/F control, the proposed control scheme improves the stability of the motor, and realizes the approximate maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) control under scalar control.

articleTitle: Acceleration of Electric Machine Structure optimization Using Performance Classifier Enhanced Evolutionary Search
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The optimization of electric machine structure can be highly time-consuming, as it often involves an evolutionary search that needs to evaluate numerous samples. Each sample requires computationally intensive finite element analysis (FEA). In this paper, a stacked classification model along with a class-balanced dataset is used to build classifiers of Key Performance Indicator (KPI). These classifiers are used to predict coarse levels of KPIs for structure samples. The structure samples that are classified as inferior with respect to the optimization objectives will not perform expensive FEA simulations, thereby accelerating the search process. To demonstrate its effectiveness, the proposed method is applied to optimize a V-shaped permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) with practical constraints. In the single-objective optimization cases, the proposed method can reduce the computation cost by up to 60% compared to the standard Genetic Algorithm (GA). In the multi-objective optimization cases that balances torque maximization and torque ripple minimization, the Pareto frontier is also improved compared to the standard Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II (NSGA-II).

articleTitle: Control Strategy Research on Charge Balancing of Hybrid Energy Storage Units with Islanded Operation Mode of DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: When DC microgrid operates in islanded mode, the hybrid energy storage units (HESUs) can maintain voltage stability and energy balance if load fluctuates or distributed generation (DG) output fluctuates by charging and discharging. To improve the stability and duration of microgrid operation in islanded mode, a hybrid energy storage system (HESS) of Nickel-Metal-Hydride battery and supercapacitor is adopted in this paper. Based on DC-DC conversion circuit, Nickel-Metal-Hydride battery compensates for the low-frequency part of power, and supercapacitor compensates for the high-frequency part of power. Aiming at the unbalanced state of charge (SOC) caused by uneven power distribution of HESUs, an improved droop control strategy considering line impedance is designed. The power distribution of each unit is adjusted in real time by detecting the SOC and the state of converter output current in each hybrid energy storage unit (HESU), and finally the SOC of each unit is consistent. A hybrid energy storage microgrid system is built based on Matlab/Simulink, and the proposed control strategy is verified. The results show that the control strategy can stabilize the DC bus voltage not only in normal operation but also under one HESU fault, and realize the balanced distribution of current load among the units.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control of a Novel Isolated Radial Active Magnetic Bearing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: A new type of isolated active magnetic bearing (IAMB) with isolation sleeve is studied. The stator and rotor are completely isolated and can work in different environment respectively. The application range of traditional active magnetic bearing (AMB) is expanded effectively. According to the structural particularity of IAMB magnetic circuit, the equivalent magnetic circuit considering the reluctance of the isolation sleeve is established and the magnetic circuit matrix is given. According to the magnetic leakage effect of the isolation sleeve, a method to determine the current operating point of the IAMB was proposed based on the magnetic density variation characteristics of the isolation sleeve and rotor. The eddy current of the isolation sleeve aggravates the hysteresis of the system. In order to balance the lead performance of the control system and restrain the noise of the system, the incomplete differential PID controller is designed to control the rotor position. Finally, the experiment platform was built and the suspension experiment and anti-interference experiment were designed to verify the feasibility of the IAMB system and the correctness of the analysis.

articleTitle: Analysis on the speed regulation performance of an adjustable-speed permanent magnet eddy-current coupling with a double-layer permanent magnet rotor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper bases on a novel adjustable-speed permanent magnet eddy-current coupling with a double-layer permanent magnet rotor, the output characteristics, speed regulation performance, and the influence of structural parameters are studied, respectively. The structure and working principle are introduced, and the feasibility is verified by calculating the air gap flux density and output torque when the double-layer permanent magnet rotor at different relative positions. Then the output speed characteristic and speed regulation performance are respectively studied when a fan load is applied on permanent magnet rotor. And finally, the influence of structural parameters on speed regulation performance is also researched, including the material of the conductor layer, the thickness of copper layer, and material of permanent magnet.

articleTitle: Shafts Influence on Permanent Magnet Magnetization for V-Type Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Post-assembly magnetization (PAM) has been widely adopted when manufacturing permanent magnet (PM) electrical machines to simplify the assembly process. However, for V-type interior PM synchronous machines (IPMSMs), magnetizing the bottom of V-type PMs is challenging. This paper investigates the shaft influence of PAM by comparing the results with three different shafts. Eddy currents within the shafts are considered and found impactful for magnetization. Simulation results show that the PAM requires less energy consumption with the machine shaft than without any shaft, and the PAM with the dummy shaft is even better as the eddy currents are suppressed. Finally, experimental validation is conducted with a magnetization fixture of various capacitances.

articleTitle: Design and Comparative Study of a Novel Double-Rotor Vernier Permanent Magnet Machine for Wind Tower Tuned Mass Damper Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel double-rotor vernier permanent magnet machine (DRVPMM) for potential application in wind tower tuned mass damper (TMD) systems. The impact of wind-induced loads on wind towers exhibits time variabilities. Therefore, the DRVPMM is set to operate in three different working states. Considering the varying performance requirements of the DRVPMM under different operating conditions, a multi-objective optimization of the DRVPMM’s structure is proposed, based on the co-simulation between Ansys-Maxwell and Optislang software. Firstly, the optimization objectives are set to maximize efficiency, minimize torque ripple, and maximize output torque. Secondly, Evolutionary algorithms (EA) are used to optimize the machine parameters and the objectives set on three different working states. Thirdly, select candidate cases that meet all three working states simultaneously. Finally, a weighted function is used for the final selection of candidate cases. Based on the proposed design method, the optimized machine meets the requirements of the TMD system.

articleTitle: Differential Mode and Common Mode Coupling Analysis and Robust Design of Three Phase Four Bridge
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The three-phase four-bridge (3P4B) inverter has been widely used in unbalanced load compensation and emergency power supply. However, unlike the widely studied three-phase three-bridge (3P3B) inverter, the 3P4B suffers from common-mode stability problems under different grid impendence due to the existence of the fourth bridge. To address this issue, this paper firstly establishes the differential-mode (DM) and common-mode (CM) equivalent circuit models of the 3P4B, revealing the essential reasons for the CM stability problem. Then, starting from the maximum and minimum resonant frequency under wide varying grid impedance, a CM circuit design scheme is proposed. This scheme can keep the 3P4B stable under arbitrary grid impedance. Finally, this paper demonstrates the correctness of the design scheme through simulation.

articleTitle: Research on Flux-Weakening and DC-link Voltage Compensation of PMSM Drive System without Electrolytic Capacitor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The permanent magnet synchronous motor drive system without electrolytic capacitors using small capacitance capacitors is a research hotspot in the field of household appliances. This article proposes a flux-weakening control strategy for a permanent magnet synchronous motor drive system without electrolytic capacitors. It is based on the equivalent current power-tracking method, taking into account the fluctuation range of DC bus voltage and speed, to obtain the expected value of the d-axis current. This results in good power and speed tracking effect, while improving the power factor on the grid side and reducing the amplitude of bus overvoltage during startup. Secondly, when the DC-link voltage fluctuates to a low point below the back electromotive force of the motor, it will affect the current control effect and cause the DC-link voltage to rise or even overvoltage. A DC-link voltage compensation control strategy is proposed, which proportionally compensates for the expected voltage output from the current loop, achieving a reduction in the rise and fluctuation amplitude of the DC-link voltage. Finally, a simulation model was established, and the effectiveness of the algorithm was verified by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Simplified Computation Model of Efficiency Map For Low-Speed and High-Torque PM Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a computation model for efficiency map in a low-speed and high-torque permanent-magnet synchronous machine without magnetic bridge. According to the magnetic field distribution, the whole machine topology is then divided into seven types of subdomains. By means of the magnetic field prediction and classic loss model, different losses and electromagnetic torques of motor under different working conditions are obtained, and finally the full analytical calculation of the motor efficiency in the all working domain is realized. The impact of rotor saturation is analyzed by establishing a local polar coordinate system. Then a program is used to build efficiency map. Results from Finite Elements Analysis (FEA) are used to verify the proposed method.

articleTitle: Enhancing Safety and Dynamic Control in Hub Motor Electric Vehicles through ASC and PIR Current Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Hub motor electric vehicles are a revolutionary technology that integrates electric motors into the wheel hubs, offering efficient power transmission and motion control. The increasing demand for hub motor electric vehicle performance has led to the development of fault tolerance and self-recovery technologies, particularly concerning safety. This paper addresses dynamic control issues and proposes a Proportional Integral-Resonance (PIR) closed-loop current controller for hub motors, specifically to suppress surge current after active short-circuit (ASC) engagement. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of the PIR control strategy in controlling surge current and improving vehicle stability during hub motor restarts. The simulation study showcases the benefits of PIR control over conventional PI control in terms of current tracking accuracy and dynamic response. The results indicate that PIR control significantly reduces signal amplitude errors, ensuring smoother operation and improved dynamic performance.

articleTitle: Dynamic modeling and performance prediction of hysteresis motors considering material properties
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Hysteresis motors have attracted much attention in many aspects due to their excellent operating characteristics. However, the problem of establishing an accurate dynamic model of hysteresis motor always limits its application in closed-loop control, and the previous modeling based on constant impedance does not consider the effect of load variation on the motor characteristics, which results in low accuracy. In this paper, the influence of material properties on motor characteristics is considered based on variable impedance-based modeling, which improves the accuracy of the motor model in the full dynamic response process; on this basis, the performance of the motor can be predicted.

articleTitle: Torque Improvement by Injecting Third Harmonics in Flux Reversal Permanent Magnet Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Flux reversal permanent magnet (PM) (FRPM) machines are popular for the high torque density and low PM usage, as well as the robustness. In order to further improve the torque while mitigate the torque ripple, both sinusoidal arc PMs and sinusoidal superimposed by 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> harmonics arc PMs are evaluated on FRPM machines in this paper. By employing finite element (FE) tool, the impacts on PM dimensions and 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> harmonic ratio are analyzed for the two shaped PMs. Moreover, three FRPM machines employing conventional arc-shaped PMs, sinusoidal arc PMs, and sinusoidal superimposed by3rd harmonics arc PMs, are comprehensively compared, with particular reference to their flux distributions, back electromotive force waveforms, cogging torques, average torques, and torque ripples. It is revealed that the sinusoidal superimposed by 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> harmonics arc PMs contribute to 7.2% higher torques whilst 24% lower torque ripples compared with conventional arc-shaped PMs.

articleTitle: Efficiency and Starting Torque Improvement by Optimizing Rotor Dimensions Based on Response Surface Methodology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Submersible induction machines (SIMs) connected with pumps require high efficiency and reliability for their special use. Nevertheless, the efficiency optimization process of SIMs may lead to poor mechanical performance. To balance the electrical and mechanical performance, response surface methodology is used to model and optimize the SIMs. The electrical and mechanical optimization processes are combined by utilizing weigh factors. The optimization results are verified by finite element analysis.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Characteristic Analysis and Design of a Novel Intensifying-Flux Hybrid Excited Permanent Magnet Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel intensifying-flux hybrid excitation machine (IF-HEPMSM) is proposed in conjunction with the latest development requirements of electric vehicles. Therefore, the proposed IF-HEPMSM design can simultaneously obtain the synergy of strong overload capability and wide speed regulation range. Firstly, the topology, characteristics and working principle of IF-HEPMSM are introduced to reveal the improvement of the machine performance, based on which, the tooth width and yoke thickness of the machine stator are optimized to ensure the output torque of the machine while effectively improving the wide flux regulation range. The electromagnetic characteristics of the IF-HEPMSM are investigated and compared with the IF-PMSM, conventional permanent magnet machine to highlight the superiority of the IF-HEPMSM.

articleTitle: Speed Control Based on an Improved PID Controller with BP Neural Network for Two Wheel Differential AGV System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The motor of Automatic Guided Vehicle (AGV) has characteristics of nonlinearity, time-varying uncertainty, strong interference, traditional PID control algorithms are difficult to achieve ideal control effects. To address this issue, this paper proposes an improved PID control method based on backpropagation (BP) neural network and incorporating inertia factors. The error between the expected speed and actual speed of the AGV left and right wheels is used as input to the BP neural network to adjust the parameters of the PID controller and improve the speed control accuracy of the AGV. The simulation results validate the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based Feedforward Compensation Control in PMSM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper presents a Proximal Policy optimization(PPO) feedforward compensation algorithm based on reinforcement learning for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM).
