The PPO algorithm eliminates the need for precise system modeling and achieves lower steady-state errors and improved generalization capabilities through adaptive optimization training. Additionally, we introduce modules to enhance the performance of the PPO algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the PPO feedforward control in reducing speed fluctuations and stabilizing the motor’s operation near the target speed.

articleTitle: Voltage Harmonic Reduction of Cascaded H-bridge Multilevel Inverter Based on SHEPWM by Using Optimized Immune Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The utilization of Selected Harmonic Elimination Pulse Width Modulation (SHEPWM) technology poses a significant challenge in addressing nonlinear equations due to its inherent complexity. To tackle this specific issue, this paper integrates the Immune Algorithm (IA) with SHEPWM. The IA, implemented using MATLAB, was employed to compute the modeling results for qualified switching angles. The simulation outcomes demonstrate that the application of IA in SHEPWM surpasses other algorithms in terms of Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) reduction and the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) of line voltage in eliminating harmonics of a cascaded H-bridge multilevel inverter. This superiority arises from its enhanced performance in convergence rate and its ability to address local optima.

articleTitle: An orderly charging strategy for electric vehicles in residential areas with limited power infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: As a clean and low-carbon travel tool, the number of electric vehicles (EVs)is growing rapidly year by year. However, the random charging behaviors of abundant EVs will lead to some problems in residential areas with limited power infrastructure, such as electric equipment overload and increased load peak-valley difference. To solve these problems, this paper proposes an orderly charging strategy for EVs in residential areas with limited power infrastructure. Firstly, a charging model for EVs is constructed considering the daily mileage, return time, and initiation time. Moreover, an EV orderly charging strategy is proposed based on the mixed integer linear programming method (MILP). In the strategy, charging cost and peak-valley difference are modeled as two optimization objects. Finally, simulations and analysis are given to verify the effectiveness of the strategy.

articleTitle: Design of Integrated Experimental Platform for Power Electronics Based on TMS320F28335
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: A digital experimental platform for the teaching of the “Power Electronics Technology” course has been developed based on DSP TMS320F28335. The design scheme is that the three-phase inverter function and the DC chopper function are integrated in the hardware circuit, The control algorithm and program for each experimental project have also been integrated to facilitate the completion of corresponding experimental projects by switching different modes. The detailed design of the hardware circuits of each main module is introduced, and the experimental waveforms of Buck and Boost voltage chopper, single-phase square wave and three-phase square wave inversion, single-phase sine wave and three-phase sine wave inversion were provided. This integrated experimental platform has very powerful functions and basically meets the experimental need of “Power Electronics Technology” course. it will been optimized and expanded to related experiments in motor control.

articleTitle: Study on Electromagnetic Noise Reduction of Induction Machines by Rotor Notch Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Reducing electromagnetic noise is a prominent area of research in induction machines. When parameters are changed to reduce noise, the performance of the machine may also be affected. In this paper, the method of rotor slot notching was used to reduce electromagnetic vibration and acoustic noise. Firstly, the analytical formula of radial electromagnetic force of induction machine is derived. Then, taking an 1120kW machine as the research object, the electromagnetic force distribution is analyzed. A method to weaken the magnitude of the electromagnetic force by slotting in the rotor is proposed, and a fitting mathematical model of the size of the rotor slot notch and the extent of the electromagnetic force is established. The particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm was used to modify the size of the rotor slot notches. Finally, the results show that the noise is reduced by 5.67 dB and the efficiency of the machine is basically unchanged, which verifies the method’s effectiveness.

articleTitle: A Novel Parallel Magnetic Circuit Variable Flux Machine by Employing Flux Leakage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel parallel magnetic circuit variable flux machine by employing flux leakage paths (PMC-VFMFLP), improving the torque density, flux regulation range, and speed operation range of conventional PMC-VFMs with flux barriers. Both the high coercivity force (HCF) and low coercivity force (LCF) permanent magnets (PMs) are applied in this machine. The key to the proposed machine design lies in the position of flux leakage paths and the relative parameters of the two kinds of PMs. The finite-element analysis (FEA) is adopted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed machine. The FEA results indicate that a high torque density, a wide flux regulation range, and wide manipulate range with high efficiency can be obtained by the proposed machine simultaneously.

articleTitle: Harmonic Current Suppression Method Based on PCC Voltage and Capacitor Voltage Feedforward for Virtual Synchronous Generator in Distorted Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: For distributed generation systems, virtual synchronous generators (VSGs) can reduce the inertia of the overall power system. However, the distorted grid voltage degrades the quality of VSG grid-connected currents, and the existing methods based on PCC voltage feedforward are limited due to the effect of voltage control bandwidth on the equivalent impedance. To address this issue, this paper reveals the relationship between the grid-connected harmonic currents and the distorted grid voltage, and explains the essential causes of harmonic current generation. This paper feeds forward the capacitor voltage and PCC voltage in a specific proportion to obtain the real grid distortion voltage information, which can eliminate the influence of distortion voltage on the output current quality. Moreover, the output impedance is further improved to solve the limitations of existing methods. Finally, a comparative simulation is carried out, and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed method.

articleTitle: Fault Redundancy Active Removal Fault-tolerant Strategy for Triple-redundancy PMSMs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The reliability requirements of the aviation electromechanical actuator system are high, and the three-redundancy motor is often used to provide reliable propulsion power. The triple-redundancy PMSMs is composed of a nine-phase stator winding and a permanent magnet rotor. When a redundancy fails, the fault redundancy is actively removed, and the use of other redundancy can still maintain the normal operation of the system to ensure that the entire system can maintain normal operation. However, the traditional 3-dq modeling method ignores the mutual inductance and flux linkage coupling between different windings, and it is difficult to achieve a smooth transition of redundancy removal. The purpose of this paper is to propose a decoupling control method for multi-stator modeling, which eliminates the cross-coupling of mutual inductance between redundancy and retains the modular control characteristics of 3-dq decoupling. When one or two redundant faults occur, the fault winding is actively removed to reduce the dynamic transition time of speed and torque during redundancy switching and realize the smooth transition of fault winding removal.

articleTitle: Online Estimation of Transient Temperature of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based On LPTN
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: High motor temperature in a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) will lead to motor performance degradation, life-shortening, and other problems, so it is necessary to carry out a thermal analysis of the motor. When controlling the motor, control strategies such as field weakening control and position sensorless control are inseparable from the stator winding resistance and magnetic chain parameters, which are greatly affected by temperature, so it is necessary to monitor the transient temperature of the motor in real-time. 3-, 4-, 5-, and 6-node LPTN (lumped-parameter thermal network) models are established according to the motor loss model, the model parameters are identified by particle swarm optimization (PSO), and the motor temperature curves are calculated online based on the models of different nodes under the variable operating conditions, finally, and the simulation results of the models with different nodes are compared with the experimental data. It is found that, when the number of nodes is five, during the whole experimental process, the temperature error between the estimated temperature of the windings and stator and the experimental temperature is minimized, and the temperature error is always within 5.42°C.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Nonlinear Characteristics of Oil Paper Insulation in Oil Immersed Power Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This article proposes an equivalent circuit model for the nonlinear characteristics of oil-paper insulation under dielectric response tests. Using Simulink software, the equivalent circuit model was validated, and the consistency between simulation results and measured results was compared, providing ideas and basis for subsequent research on the nonlinear characteristics of oil-paper insulation.

articleTitle: Iterative Learning Algorithm with Adaptive Forgetting Function for Suppressing Compressor Torque Ripple
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Torque ripple is an important concern in air conditioning compressor systems operating at low frequencies. An algorithm for suppressing compressor torque ripple is proposed to address the problems of significant torque ripple. This iterative learning algorithm with an adaptive forgetting function is applied to the speed loop, improving the learning ability under different operating frequencies. The optimal parameter configurations are achieved by analyzing control system discretization. Meanwhile, A reduced-order state observer is included to eliminate non-periodic disturbances and enhance system stability. And the output of the proposed algorithm is compensated to the given current in the q-axis The algorithm is validated on an experimental platform for air conditioning compressors, Experimental results show that the algorithm can significantly reduce the compressor torque ripple.

articleTitle: An Improved Multi-Vector Model Predictive Torque Control Based on Virtual Voltage Vector
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper proposes an improved multi-vector model predictive torque control (MPTC) method based on virtual voltage vector (VVV) for dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor (DTP-PMSM), which optimizes the determination of the reference voltage vector (RVV) and expands the vector range by applying multiple voltage vectors. Firstly, RVV is calculated based on the o-p stator flux coordinate system, thereby achieving accurate vector calculation and high torque tracking performance. Furthermore, the number of candidates is brought down from 12 to 5. Secondly, two VVVs and a null vector are chosen to synthesize each candidate voltage vector, extending the synthesis range to the whole plane, which realizes the flexible adjustment of the amplitude and phase of the effective voltage vectors. Experimental results are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed MPTC method.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Optimization of Novel Flux-Concentrating Spoke-Type IPM Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel spoke-type interior permanent magnet (IPM) machine featuring a flux-concentrating rotor. Its primary objectives are to increase the utilization of PM material and decrease leakage flux. The evolution of the proposed flux-concentrating PM from the spoke-type PM is presented, which demonstrates a higher PM utilization ratio on torque characteristics. To achieve a high-performance design, a multi-objective genetic algorithm (MOGA) is employed for design optimization. This optimization process focuses on maximizing PM material utilization while minimizing torque ripple. The optimized machine configuration is designed to reduce copper loss and enhance efficiency by reducing current density while maintaining a similar average torque to that of the spoke-type machine. The paper utilizes finite element analysis (FEA) to compare the electromagnetic characteristics of the two machines. The results show that the proposed structure improves efficiency by 1.2% and reduces PM volume by approximately 4% in comparison to the spoke-type machine.

articleTitle: A Study about the Influence of Rotor Position of IPMSM on the Maximum Voltage on Motor Terminals under Inverter-fed Operation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this research, a comprehensive method is developed to study the influence of rotor positions on motor terminal overvoltage in interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) under inverter-fed operation. The developed approach helps understand the intricate interactions between inverters, cables, and electrical machines. In order to analyze the interactions, highly accurate grey box models for both the IPMSM and power cables are required. In developing the model, the asymmetry between phases caused by the interior permanent magnets in the IPMSM is considered. The relative errors in the developed motor model are less than 4% for all rotor position regarding the impedance modeling. Additionally, the cable model considers the frequency-dependent mutual inductances among various phases and outer shields, which is not found in the state-of-the-art. With the help of the established motor and cable models, the influence of rotor positions on the differential mode overvoltage at motor terminals is studied. The relative difference in the peak voltage values at the motor terminals is less than 5 % at different rotor positions under inverter-fed operations.

articleTitle: Analysis and Optimization of a Novel Dual-Permanent-Magnet Machine with Hybrid Teeth
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel dual-permanent-magnet motor (DPMM) with hybrid-stator-teeth structure is proposed. With hybrid stator teeth, the number of flux modulation poles can be more flexible and the relation between modulation poles and stator slots can be extended. A general slot/pole combination equation for this kind of DPMM is concluded. The conventional slot/pole combination between stator slots and rotor poles of the DPMM can be broken and more flexible slot/pole combination can be realized. One model with hybrid stator teeth based on the concluded equation is taken as an example and its performances, including airgap flux density, output torque, torque ripple, torque/PM volume, loss distribution, and efficiency, are analyzed in detail. Moreover, a traditional split teeth DPMM with the same stator slots and winding pole pairs will be optimized and the performances of the proposed motor and the traditional one will be compared. The results show that the hybrid teeth motor can maintain comparable performances to the split tooth motor with reduced permanent magnet usage. The effectiveness of the motor design is verified through simulation and comparative study.

articleTitle: AC Copper Loss Analysis of Hairpin Windings for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Considering Eddy Current Effects
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: With the increasing demand for high efficiency and power density of motors in the context of electrified transportation, hairpin windings have become a popular trend for designers. This study offers a design method which is aimed to reduce the AC copper losses generated when using hairpin windings in permanent magnet synchronous motors, and specifically deal with the effects of skin effect and proximity effect on conductor AC copper losses. On this basis, the influence of conductor dimensions, different parallel branch numbers, and slot dimensions on AC copper losses is systematically investigated. The research findings indicate that a properly designed hairpin winding topology can effectively reduce the AC copper losses of permanent magnet synchronous motors, thereby improving motor efficiency and power density.

articleTitle: Modeling for Capacitive Shaft voltage of EV Drive System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This article firstly models high-frequency and low-frequency signals based on their different characteristics, and then proposes a model and an estimation method for predicting the capacitive shaft voltage of electric vehicle electric drive systems without power supply. Then, based on the shaft voltage model, the influence of two mainstream transmissions is further considered, and an equivalent circuit model of the transmission is established, which can obtain the shaft voltage estimation of the transmission shaft and motor shaft, and realize the shaft voltage modeling and calculation of the overall drive system of electric vehicles. Finally, the paper compares the simulation waveform of the shaft voltage of the transmission shaft and motor shaft of the two transmissions, providing a reference for the selection of transmissions in the electric drive system of electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Detection and Classification of Eccentricity and High-Resistance Connection Faults in PMSMs Using Zero-Sequence Voltage Component
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Eccentricity and high-resistance connection (HRC) are two common faults in permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs). This article focuses on the detection and classification of these two faults using zero-sequence voltage component (ZSVC) in PMSMs with rotationally asymmetric winding configurations. The theoretical analysis of ZSVC under fault modes shows that the fundamental component can be introduced by HRC or static eccentricity (SE), and sideband harmonics show up under dynamic eccentricity (DE). Both the fault characteristic components appear under mixed eccentricity (ME). Especially for SE and HRC, the different fault indicators are proposed for discernment under specific working conditions, according to the different variation trend of fault harmonic amplitude with rotor speed and stator current. Finally, the simulation is conducted to verify the effectiveness of the diagnosis method.

articleTitle: High Torque Density Design For Direct Drive PM Machine Using Hybrid Pole Rotor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The torque density of traditional consequent-pole permanent magnet (PM) (CPM) machines is difficult to improve unless PM materials with higher remanence density are used. Therefor, a novel hybrid-pole permanent magnet (HPM) rotor is designed in this paper. The staggered PM sequence enhances the magnetic field aggregation ability and the utilization rate of PM materials, which enables HPM machine to meet the requirements of high torque density direct drive application. In addition, the electromagnetic performances of the proposed machine, including the open-circuit airgap flux density, back EMF, cogging torque, average torque, overload capacity, and efficiency, were compared with traditional machines. It is demonstrated that the utilization ratio of PM in HPMM can be increased by up to 17%, and the torque density is comparable to spoke-type permanent magnet (STPM) machine.

articleTitle: A Three-Port DC-DC Power Converter Based on GaN Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The cascaded interleaved bidirectional Buck/Boost LLC Three-port DC-DC converter has the advantages of wide voltage input range, Zero-Voltage-Switching (ZVS) on the primary side and low input current ripple. The three-port converter can be categorized into five distinct operational modes and three power transmission modes. This paper takes a operational mode as a representative example to analyze its operational characteristics and employs the time-domain analysis technique to derive the voltage gain curves. The application of Gallium Nitride (GaN) power devices to the converter is expected to further reduce the volume and improve the efficiency. In this paper, an RC+regulated diode driver circuit is used to drive GaN power semiconductors with advantages of high-speed safety switch and negative level turn-off. Finally, a 15W cascaded interleaved bidirectional Buck/Boost LLC three-port DC-DC converter experimental platform based on GaN is built.

articleTitle: Reducing Cogging Torque and Torque Ripple in Dual-Stator Permanent Magnet Vernier Motor by changing Rotor Rib Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper has researched on a dual-stator permanent magnet vernier motor’s cogging torque and torque ripple analysis for a wind turbine. Because beginning torque lowers generating power in generator mode, it’s crucial to reduce cogging torque and torque ripple. The attraction between the steel teeth of the stator laminations and the permanent magnets installed on the rotor is an important factor to cogging torque. The thickness of the rotor’s ribs could be a factor that is studied to determine whether it has an impact on cogging torque and torque ripple. Both cogging torque and torque ripple reducing effect factors are suggested. Moreover, verifying the characteristics of torque ripple and cogging torque through experiment.

articleTitle: Study on the over-advance angle weakening control of inverted salient pole leakage controllable PMSM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The mathematical model for this new motor type is derived based on the inverted salient pole feature of the inductance in the straight axis of the inverted salient pole leakage magnetically controllable permanent magnet synchronous motor, which is larger than the cross-axis inductance, and the controllable leakage magnetism of the straight axis. According to current trajectory characteristics, weak magnetic areas in the inverted salient pole leakage controllable permanent magnet synchronous motor are distributed in both the magnetizing area and the weak magnetic area of the second quadrant of the intersecting straight axis. Designing an appropriate initial weak magnetic angle and combining it with the voltage error-derived over-advance angle allows for weak magnetic control of the aforementioned areas. Furthermore, adjusting the orthogonal axis current component also contributes to effective weak magnetic control. Technical abbreviations will be explained when first used. After conducting a Simulink simulation, the results align with the theoretical analysis, confirming the validity and feasibility of implementing the inverse convex pole leakage controlled permanent magnet synchronous motor’s weak magnetism over-advance angle.

articleTitle: Comparison of Core Loss Models Considering the Impact of PWM Switching
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Static power electronic converters driven by pulse-width modulation (PWM) cause extra losses in electrical machine laminations. This paper compares various Bertotti methods for computing core losses at different switching frequencies, modulation indices, and flux densities. These loss models are implemented by extracting the magnetic field results of a time-stepping finite element model and analysing the field with frequency/time-domain Bertotti method. An Epstein frame setup is developed using litz wire and non-grain oriented steel to validate these loss models. The measurements with sinusoidal supply show that both frequency-domain and time-domain Bertotti method (FBM) have decent accuracy when the flux density is no less than 0.5 T. The measurements with PWM voltage supply show that the direct implementation of either frequency-domain or time-domain Bertotti methods can lead to large errors, and the indirect frequency-domain Bertotti method has the best accuracy among all the four methods investigated. These investigations reveal the inherent limitations of the frequency-domain and time-domain Bertotti methods.

articleTitle: Simulation Model for Loss Measurement of Electrical Steel and Study on the Influence of Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In order to calculate the motor core loss accurately, it is usually necessary to test the loss characteristics of the electrical steel (silicon steel), including the specific loss under different frequencies and different flux densities, that is, the loss per unit volume or unit weight. Some samples of specific shapes need to be made before testing, and the testing is time-consuming. The finite element simulation can be used to replace the testing work to a certain extent, thus reducing the material cost and labor cost. In this paper, a simulation model for annular silicon steel sheet is constructed, and its accuracy is verified by comparing with the tested results. On this basis, the influence of flux density harmonics on core loss can be studied.

articleTitle: Optimal Slot-Pole Combination of In-Wheel BLDC Motor for High Performance Personal Mobility
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this paper, design on the slot-pole combinations of BLDC motor was presented to improve performance such as efficiency and cogging torque. The three slot-pole combinations that have the high winding factor and maintain the balanced phase conditions, including conventional slot-pole combination, were selected and the loss distributions were analyzed by using Finite Element Method (FEM). Finally, the optimal slot-pole combination that has better performance than conventional model was derived.

articleTitle: Comparison and Analysis of Photovoltaic Load Shedding and Frequency Regulation Strategies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: With the rapid development of photovoltaic (PV) technology, the global installed capacity is continuously increasing. However, several considerations regarding PV grid integration exist, such as maximum power point tracking (MPPT) control for PV electricity generation and power balancing during grid integration. This paper systematically introduces the principles of PV MPPT control and methods for load frequency control in PV grid integration, including droop control, virtual synchronous machine-based virtual inertia control, and DC-side capacitance-based virtual inertia control. To validate the performance, we built a simulation model using Simulink and conducted simulations under large and small disturbances in grid load. Based on the simulation results, each of the three methods has its characteristics and needs to be combined in practical applications.

articleTitle: Accurate Prediction of Efficiency Region of Permanent Magnet Machines Based on Magnetic-Thermal Coupling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The operating temperature of the motor has a significant impact on electromagnetic performance, which affects in efficiency prediction. This article adopts a magnetic thermal bidirectional coupling method to obtain accurate operating temperature and corresponding electromagnetic performance with the consideration of dynamic changes of material thermal characteristics. Based on the results of finite element analysis (FEA), a dependence factor is developed to compare the different temperature dependencies of the motor loss and torque. Then, the relationship that the highest efficiency point of the motor under different working conditions occurs at different temperatures is obtained, which can provide guidance for the design of motor heat dissipation system. Finally, an efficiency prediction model considering temperature is established, and improve the accuracy comparing with the traditional method.

articleTitle: Day-ahead scheduling study of temperature-controlled load participation in wind power consumption
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: As the proportion of new energy continues to expand, new energy prediction deviation represented by wind power will lead to increased uncertainty of power output on the generation side, while temperature-controlled loads such as residential air conditioning and central air conditioning are high-quality dispatchable resources. This paper establishes a load aggregation model for residential air conditioning and a virtual energy storage model for central air conditioning in response to wind power prediction deviation. It also constructs an optimal dispatch model of virtual power plant with temperature-controlled loads, and proposes a control strategy for temperature-controlled loads to weaken the wind power prediction error with the goal of maximising the consumption of wind power deviation power.

articleTitle: Demagnetization Analysis of Surface-Mounted Permanent-Magnet Synchronous Machine Based on Subdomain Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: We present a model of demagnetization of surface-mounted permanent-magnet (PM) machines (SMPMMs) based on a subdomain model. The PM volume demagnetization percentage is calculated at different current densities and rotation angles. In this research, we study the demagnetization error as a function of the size of the matrix resulting from the subdomain model and the finite element method (FEM) to evaluate the advantage of the subdomain model in terms of computational resources. In our machine, compared with the FEM, the matrix size decreases by 15 times and the average error of the subdomain model is less than 1.2%. The subdomain model is hence a helpful tool for quick preoptimization of SMPMMs.

articleTitle: Analytical Model for No-Load Rotor Bracket Loss of Axial flux Hybrid Excitation Motor based on Subdomain Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Due to the drawbacks of high computational complexity and long time consumption when calculating the loss of the rotor bracket using three-dimensional finite element method, this paper proposes a field coupling analysis method based on subdomain method and circuit equations to calculate the loss of the no-load rotor bracket of a composite axial hybrid excitation motor. Firstly, the motor is divided into air gap subdomains and slot subdomains adjacent to the ferromagnetic poles. The DC excitation winding is equivalent to the current sheet located at the junction of the air gap subdomain and the inner diameter of the stator. The subdomain method is used to analyze and calculate the air gap magnetic field of the motor. Due to the relative motion of the fixed rotor, the magnetic field in the rotor bracket changes, resulting in the generation of induced electromotive force in the rotor bracket. The rotor bracket is equivalent to a network model of resistors, and the resistance network method is used to calculate the losses of the rotor bracket. Finally, the correctness of the analytical model for rotor support loss was verified through a no-load excitation experiment of a composite axial hybrid excitation motor.

articleTitle: A DITC Method With Copper loss Minimum During Commutation Region of Bearingless Switched Reluctance Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In the paper, a control strategy based on direct instantaneous torque control (DITC) is proposed to suppress the torque ripple and reduce the copper loss of bearingless switched reluctance motor (BSRM) during commutation region. A sharing suspension windings bearingless switched reluctance motor (SSWBSRM) is taken as research objective in the paper. The mathematical model of SSW-BSRM in non-overlapped region between stator pole and rotor pole is derived, which better reveals the characteristics of torque and suspension force during commutation region. The correctness of the proposed model is verified by comparing with the finite element analysis results. According to the difference in torque and suspension force generated by the currents of outgoing phase and incoming phase during commutation region, both the currents of torque winding and suspension winding are modulated. With the optimization objective of minimizing the square of the current (copper loss), each current is optimized based on the Lagrange multiplier method. The simulation on a three-phase 12/8 SSW-BSRM by comparing with current chopping control (CCC) validate the performance of the proposed control strategy. The simulation results show that the proposed control strategy can suppress the torque ripple and reduce the copper loss of BSRM.

articleTitle: Research on Risk Assessment and Fault Location Method for Relay Protection Equipment in Intelligent Substation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Relay protection equipment is an important defense line in the power system. It is necessary to conduct special research on the reliability, risk assessment, and fault location of intelligent substation relay protection equipment to improve the reliability of relay protection equipment and ensure the reliability of power system operation. This article proposes a fast and accurate method for fault location of relay protection equipment to ensure the reliability of relay protection equipment operation and to ensure its reliability. Quickly and accurately locate and handle faults to reduce the risk of faults. Firstly, a reliability model was constructed using Markov, which can effectively obtain the real-time state probability distribution of each RPE. Secondly, a severity model for the corresponding indicators was established using a mixed utility function to describe the risk consequences. Finally, a fault location model for relay protection equipment was constructed using a matrix algorithm and BPNN. At the same time, the logical relationship and state analysis formula between each state of the secondary system were combined, and the BPNN model was used to optimize the shortcomings of the matrix algorithm. Simulation and example analysis results showed that the method achieved the expected requirements for fault location of protection equipment.

articleTitle: Low Carbon-Economic Dispatch of Integrated Energy Systems Considering CHP-CCS-P2GH2 Joint Operation Under Carbon-Energy Market
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: To fully exploit the carbon reduction capacity of the integrated energy system (IES), a low-carbon economic dispatching model of the IES considering combined heating and power and carbon capture system (CHP-CCS) and a refined power-to-gas (P2G) with two-staged heating recycling (CHP-CCS-P2GH<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) under the coupling of carbon and energy market is proposed. Firstly, a flexible joint operation model of CHP-CCS and a refined two-staged P2G model are constructed. Then, the carbon trading mechanism is introduced to construct a stepped carbon trading cost model to restrict emissions. Numerical results show that the proposed model has advantages in reduce operation cost and carbon emissions, compared with existing works.

articleTitle: Nonlinear-Carrier Pulse Width Modulation: The Optimization of Wide-Range Operating Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Most converter designs overlook the potential benefits of utilizing diverse pulse width modulation (PWM) carriers, resulting in a lack of understanding of how various carriers can enhance system performance. Better performance could be achieved by employing nonlinear carriers instead of linear modulation. In this paper, a nonlinear-carrier PWM is proposed. The influence of nonlinear-carrier PWM on the system is analyzed. The proposed nonlinear-carrier PMW is used to improve the performance of the Buck converter. For any systems with nonlinear input characteristics, the linear input range of the system can be expanded using the proportionally scaled nonlinear input wave as the PWM carrier. The following content will strictly deduce the applicability, analyze nonlinear carriers’ influence on a control system, and propose a mapping relation from nonlinear input properties to nonlinear PWM carrier waves. The simulation results indicate that using nonlinear carrier PWM can enhance the linearity and global response of systems with nonlinear input characteristics.

articleTitle: Multi-objective optimization of a Brushless Hybrid Excitation Synchronous Generator Using Axial Excitation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The hybrid excitation synchronous generator has the advantages of flexible air-gap magnetic field adjustment and high power density. The multi-objective optimization of a brushless hybrid excitation synchronous generator using axial excitation is studied in this paper. The stator core loss, total harmonic distortion (THD) of output current and flux modulation coefficient are the optimization objectives of the generator. The sensitivity of the structural parameters is analyzed by Taguchi method and divided into two levels. Based on the hierarchical strategy, response surface method, genetic algorithm and single parameter scanning method are used for multi-objective optimization. In addition, the scheme is compared with the optimization scheme based on the conventional response surface model. By comparing the optimization results of the two schemes, the structural parameters with the best optimization performance of the generator are finally determined. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the optimization method are verified by the three-dimensional finite element simulation.

articleTitle: Leaning Assisted Thermal Dynamic Modeling of Air-Conditioned Building for Predictive Energy Management
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Accurate thermal dynamic model is the cornerstone for advanced temperature regulations and energy saving of modern buildings. This article deals with the multi-step prediction of the building temperature that is influenced by the residential air-conditioning systems. A smart building energy management system is first developed in a networked environment, which integrates remote climate controllers and sensors to collect real-time data related to air conditioning (AC) performance. We propose a data-driven model based on the Long-short term memory (LSTM) network to accurately capture the intertemporal temperature changes of the room under varying external conditions. The LSTM models employ piecewise affine activation functions that are beneficial for predictive management. The algorithm and system implementation leverage the strengths of MATLAB and Python, where we provide a common approach for deploying deep learning models that can be transplanted between the coding languages. The verification is carried out based on data collected from simulation and real environment, which both demonstrates the desired performance of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Non-intrusive Load Identification Method Based on Feature Optimization and Bayesian Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: With the gradual improvement of virtual power plant marketization and demand side response mechanism,the demand for accurate identification of user load power data is also increasing.The current research method lacks the discussion of the comprehensiveness and redundancy of load feature combination.This paper establishes a set of non-intrusive load monitoring and identification methods for this problem,including event detection,feature extraction,feature selection and load identification.First,the CUSUM event monitoring algorithm based on the sliding window was improved to detect the load switching events and isolate the single load information.A total of 84-dimensional load features were extracted,including steady-state current,power,harmonic features,U-I curve shape features,and transient features.Measure the correlation between features and categories and the redundancy between features.Then the Bayesian classification algorithm model is established,with the selected features as input,and the load category identification is completed.Using the publicly available dataset WHITED,the present method selects the optimal feature subset,analyzes the influence of different feature dimensions on the accuracy rate,with fast identification speed and high accuracy rate,and realizes all the functions from event monitoring to load identification.

articleTitle: Advancements in Suppressing Load Disturbances of Electric Motor Drives: An Overview
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive overview of load disturbances in electric motor systems, their impact on performance, and existing control methods. First, load disturbances that can affect motor stability, control accuracy, dynamics, and energy efficiency, including static, dynamic, and nonlinear load variations, are introduced. Second, traditional control methods used for suppressing load disturbances like feedback and feedforward control are discussed, along with their advantages and limitations. Third, advanced control strategies such as intelligent control, self-adaptive control, and robust nonlinear control are introduced. Finally, this paper highlights the need for further research and identifies future directions. Overall, this review paper contributes to the development of robust motor control strategies, enhancing industrial automation and manufacturing processes.

articleTitle: Neural Networks for Data-driven Modeling of Active Magnetic Bearing Suspended Rotor System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Active magnetic bearing (AMB) suspended rotor systems are often modeled and validated through system identification experiments, aiming to derive parametric or nonparametric models for analysis. Given the complexity of this type of system compromising non-linear electrical and speed-varying mechanical systems, neural network based prediction models are worth pursuing for to increase the modeling options. This paper addresses issues in the training of feedforward neural network (FNN) for SISO and MIMO identification cases of AMB suspended rotor system, when artificially generated excitation signals are superposed to the position controller output. Particular attention is given to the predictive capability of the trained models when applied to unseen datasets. The trained networks are validated by a test rotor system using the data collected.
